why: Re-driven at 320/390/430 on tasks.board and tasks.dense: the phone fold really is grid-template-columns: 34px minmax(0,1fr) 74px, and every one of the seat's numbers reproduced to the pixel - .lrowSay computes 116px at 320, 186px at 390, 226px at 430; 5 of 13 board rows and 17 of 32 dense rows carry .when[data-t="none"] (visibility:hidden, 0px wide) and still pay the fixed 74px track. Measured characters-per-line via Range client rects: 21.1 for undated rows at 390 and 18.8 for DATED rows - so the majority of rows are worse than the case the seat costed. Applying the seat's rule gave exactly its predicted deltas (116->198, 186->268, 226->308; 13/5/7 fewer wrapped lines) with zero .lrowSay/.lrowMeta/.lrowLane rect overlap and no sideways scroll at any width.
sharpenedFix: Ship the seat's CSS rule as written - :has() is already used 32 times in this file, and the rule is verified overlap-free and scroll-safe: inside the @media (max-width:720px) block, [data-app="tasks"] .lrow:not(:has(.when:not([data-t="none"]))) .lrowSay { grid-column: 2 / -1; }. But do not stop there and do not cost the second half as optional: it is the LARGER half. The dated rows measure 18.8 cpl at 390, worse than the undated 21.1, and the CSS rule cannot touch them. Move .when inside .lrowSay, emitted before .lrowTitle and floated right, which is precisely the shape .cardTitleRow already uses on the desk (:12105). The 'NOT FLOATED' warning at :1725 does not forbid this - it records that floating .when while it is a GRID ITEM of the subgrid takes it out of flow and it escapes the row; inside .lrowSay it is a float in a block box, the same as on a card. Do both in one change, or the list still reads at 19 characters a line for two thirds of its rows.

why: Driven at 390x844 with a touch pointer: the suite tiles measure notes/tasks/timeline at 227/271/315 (pitch 44) in Notes, 54/130/206 (pitch 76) in Tasks and 63/157/251 (pitch 94) in Timeline - every number the seat gave, exact - so the Notes tile really does travel 173px (44% of the screen) on a crossing while the avatar holds at 341-373 in all three. The cause is .railGroup { flex: 1; justify-content: space-around } at :832, so the pitch is a residue of how many per-product tools share the bar. I found it worse than the seat did: probe-tagging the DOM across a live tap proved the visible spine is a DIFFERENT NODE after the crossing - Notes shows .dock .railGroup with data-act="suite-*" tiles while Tasks and Timeline show .rail .railGroup with data-rail="*" tiles - so on a phone 'one rail, rendered once' is literally two components. The seat's one factual error: x=271 in Tasks is not bare capsule between More and Add, it is INSIDE More (box 243-287), and a stray second tap there actually operates the More door.
sharpenedFix: The seat's fix is self-contradictory and infeasible as written - it asks for '44px pitch' and 'Tasks' 54/130/206 as the ratified geometry' in the same sentence, and Tasks' pitch is 76. Worse, Tasks' span is 211px: pin that into Notes and its four 36px tools get the 113px between the spine's right edge and the avatar pinned at 341, when they need 150px, so it cannot fit at 390. Do this instead. (1) Kill the elasticity: at <=720 set .railGroup { flex: 0 0 auto; justify-content: flex-start; gap: 0 } so the three tiles are one constant 132px abutting block instead of a residue of sibling count. (2) Lay the phone bar as three parts - spine pinned left at one constant origin, per-product tools elastic in the middle, avatar pinned right - so the first tile's centre-x is one number in all three products. The compact 132px group leaves Notes 192px for its 150px of tools; verified it fits. (3) Delete one of the two spines. Until Notes stops rendering its own .dock copy with a different attribute scheme, any geometry fix has to be authored twice and will drift apart again exactly as it has.

why: Read the attributes and drove all four doors at 1440x960. [data-act="privacy"] carries aria-disabled=null and title=null, so it cannot reach the interception at :19466 that requires aria-disabled="true" AND a title matching /Not here yet/; options, photo and the account tile all carry both. Pressed and sampled at 80/250/700/1600ms: options, photo and account each paint a visible .answerPop (measured 168x54 at y=76, anchored beside the pressed control) AND announce; privacy paints nothing at any of the four times and only writes to #say. The grammar break is real too - the ratified shape is name, then 'Not here yet.', then at most one sentence of reassurance, and privacy says 'Yours until you send something on. Your privacy settings. Not here yet.', reassurance first, with that first sentence a verbatim repeat of the second half of the button's own accessible name. The file already knows this pattern: the comment at :19707 records that photo and options were REMOVED from ELSEWHERE for exactly this reason and privacy was left behind.
sharpenedFix: Confirmed the outcome, but do not use the seat's route. I applied it and read the accessibility tree: aria-disabled="true" turns the node into {role:button, name:'Private to you. Yours until you send something on.', disabled:true} - so a screen-reader user hears a TRUE, live status announced as unavailable. That is the same class of untrue statement the doors' grammar exists to prevent, and unlike the account tile (whose name already contains 'Not here yet.') this button's name is a factual claim about the note. (The seat's other risk is a non-issue: I measured the colour with and without aria-disabled and it stays rgba(17,17,17,0.72), so nothing dims.) Use the account tile's precedent at :19505 instead, which passes an explicit string and does not lean on the title interception: delete the privacy entry from the ELSEWHERE table at :19724 and add, beside the account branch, if (a === "privacy") { if (window.__SUITE && window.__SUITE.answer) window.__SUITE.answer(act, "Your privacy settings. Not here yet."); else say("Your privacy settings. Not here yet."); return; }. I ran answer() against the unmodified enabled button and it painted the identical .answerPop, 168x54 at y=76, anchored to the privacy pill - visible answer, one grammar, status left true.

why: Reproduced every branch at 1440x960 on notes.review. With the confirm up (role="status", no aria-modal, no accessible name, focus correctly on "Keep it"), pressing 't' tore the confirm down, opened the SEND peel and put focus in .peelField; 'k' filed the note and advanced 1 of 8 -> 2 of 8 announcing "Kept in Notes. 7 left."; 'l' deferred it and moved to the next note; only 'd' was a no-op. In every case the pending delete vanished with nothing said about it. The mechanism is in the source: decide() clears confirming at :16807 and the keydown handler's t/k/l branch at :20161 sits below `if (typing) return;` with no confirming guard. Tab from "Keep it" walked notebook, index row, search, account, BODY, notes, scope, privacy, options - eight stops, never back to either answer, and one of them drops activeElement to BODY entirely. I rate this blocking rather than defect because 'k' is not an off-path keystroke: it is an advertised accelerator of this exact screen, so the surface asks a destructive yes/no question and then answers a different one on the same note when a person presses a key it trained them to press. Ctrl+Z does put it back ("Put back. Kept in Notes.", queue restored to 1 of 8), which limits the data loss but not the mislead - the announcement reports ordinary success, so nothing tells her the delete was abandoned.
sharpenedFix: The seat's guard is correct and I verified it is safe where it proposes to sit: with t/k/l/j/arrows swallowed while .confirm is up, Escape still cancels (handled at :19996, above the insertion point), Enter and Space on the focused buttons still answer (native activation, not keydown-routed), and Ctrl+Z (:19896), Ctrl+K (:19939) and Ctrl+Enter (:19944) all sit above :20153 and are untouched. Two sharpenings. (1) Do not add a bare early return 180 lines down from the pattern that already exists: the file ratified this exact rule at :19972 for the picker - 'An open popup owns the keyboard ... It claims the keys before anything else reads them.' Write the confirm guard in that same shape and put it beside that block so the two modal objects read as one rule rather than two conventions. (2) role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" must not ship without the focus cycle. aria-modal on a span whose siblings are still reachable by Tab tells assistive tech the rest of the page is inert when it is not - that is a new untrue statement in place of the old one. Ship the name (aria-labelledby on the 'Delete it everywhere?' text), the role, aria-modal and the two-button Tab cycle as one change, or ship none of them. Also fix the BODY stop in the walk: focus should never leave the document.
